You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def transform(grid):
    # The small colored object is a template; each marker of the designated
    # color (5 in the demo; 9 in the test) anchors an overlaid copy.
    # Template entries relative to its anchor are copied, replacing background.
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    bg = max(set(v for row in grid for v in row), key=lambda v:sum(row.count(v) for row in grid))
    # Identify non-background colored shape around the unique compact multicolor object.
    from collections import Counter
    cnt=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row)
    colors=[v for v,n in cnt.items() if v!=bg]
    # Tiny colored template is the cluster of colors other than marker/noise.
    # Find compact 3-cell pattern by selecting non-bg colors occurring <=2.
    template=[]
    for r in range(h):
      for c in range(w):
        if grid[r][c]!=bg and grid[r][c] in colors:
          template.append((r,c,grid[r][c]))
    # determine template from non-background dense colored component: exclude singleton marker colors
    # Demo has pattern at rows 9-11 cols 0-2: [[bg,8,5],[bg,0,5],[0,7,bg]]
    # test motif rows 8-10 cols 24-26: [[bg,6,bg],[3,9,5],[bg,2,bg]]
    # Pick the most compact 3x3 window containing most distinct non-bg colors.
    best=None
    for r0 in range(h-2):
      for c0 in range(w-2):
        vals=[(r,c,grid[r][c]) for r in range(r0,r0+3) for c in range(c0,c0+3) if grid[r][c]!=bg]
        score=len(vals)
        if best is None or score>best[0]: best=(score,r0,c0,vals)
    _,ar,ac,vals=best
    # Motif marker is its center; stamp all motif non-bg cells at other marker centers.
    marker=grid[ar+1][ac+1]
    out=[row[:] for row in grid]
    for r in range(h):
      for c in range(w):
        if grid[r][c]==marker and (r,c)!=(ar+1,ac+1):
          for rr,cc,v in vals:
            y=r+(rr-(ar+1)); x=c+(cc-(ac+1))
            if 0<=y<h and 0<=x<w: out[y][x]=v
    return out
PY

def transform(grid):
    h,w=len(grid),len(grid[0]); out=[row[:] for row in grid]
    # Locate the compact 3x3 key: motif occupies a 3x3 area around its center,
    # whose color is the unique central marker (9 in test; 0 in demo).
    from collections import Counter
    bg=Counter(v for row in grid for v in row).most_common(1)[0][0]
    # use distinctive adjacent colored key-cell structure around central color
    candidates=[]
    for r in range(1,h-1):
      for c in range(1,w-1):
        # center is a non-background cell and its 8-neighborhood includes >=4 colors
        vals=[grid[y][x] for y in range(r-1,r+2) for x in range(c-1,c+2)]
        if grid[r][c]!=bg and len(set(v for v in vals if v!=bg))>=3:
          candidates.append((r,c))
    # Select marker at center of the most colorful local key.
    r0,c0=max(candidates,key=lambda p:len(set(v for y in range(p[0]-1,p[0]+2) for x in range(p[1]-1,p[1]+2) if grid[y][x]!=bg)))
    marker=grid[r0][c0]
    offsets=[(dr,dc,grid[r0+dr][c0+dc]) for dr in range(-1,2) for dc in range(-1,2) if grid[r0+dr][c0+dc]!=bg]
    # markers repeat across the field; stamp key shape centered at each marker.
    for r in range(h):
      for c in range(w):
        if grid[r][c]==marker and (r,c)!=(r0,c0):
          for dr,dc,v in offsets:
            y,x=r+dr,c+dc
            if 0<=y<h and 0<=x<w: out[y][x]=v
    return out
